SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Knee pain and clicking, mainly right knee, onset 2 weeks ago after increasing running mileage during marathon training.
  • Pain begins ≈20 min into run (≈2.5–3 miles); sometimes severe enough to stop running.  
  • Intermittent clicking noted during gym abdominal exercises requiring knee flexion-extension.  
  • Initial mild swelling after first long run responded to ice; currently no swelling, redness, or resting pain.  
  • One transient episode of tingling in right toes post-run; no persistent sensory change.
  • Denies giving way, locking, limitation of range of motion, stair or walking difficulty, calf pain, color/temperature change in legs.
- Past medical history: Hyperopia status-post LASIK surgery; previous severe UTI (treated in ED); no chronic joint disease reported.
- Medications:
  • Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented beyond occasional use)  
  • Aleve (naproxen) PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  • Vitamin D supplement  
  • Melatonin PRN  
  • Xanax (alprazolam) PRN for insomnia/anxiety (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
- Social history: Training for June marathon; plays ice hockey; attends gym several times weekly. Occasional cannabis use (“smoke a joint”). No other substances discussed.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed during video visit; therefore, no vitals or physical findings available.
- Investigations: None to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms
   - Assessment: Likely overuse/strain injury (consider patellofemoral pain syndrome or meniscal/cartilage irritation).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Ligamentous injury (e.g., ACL/MCL), meniscal tear, early osteoarthritis, bursitis.  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; may consider imaging (MRI) pending physiotherapy findings.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue ice therapy; reduce running intensity/distance; prescribe stronger NSAID (agent and dose not specified) to be taken with food, not concurrently with ibuprofen.  
   - Relevant referrals: Physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment and rehabilitation program.  

2. Transient right toe tingling
   - Assessment: Likely exercise-related neuropraxia/overuse; currently resolved.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Nerve entrapment, peripheral neuropathy, vascular insufficiency.  
   - Investigations planned: None unless symptoms recur.  
   - Treatment planned: Monitor; advise to report persistent or worsening neurological symptoms.

3. Marathon training guidance / injury prevention
   - Assessment: Over-training contributing to musculoskeletal strain.  
   - Treatment planned: Counsel to modify training schedule; emphasize gradual mileage increase, cross-training, adequate rest, and continued ice therapy; advise return if knee locks, swells, becomes red/hot, or systemic symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies, detailed medication reconciliation (doses, frequencies), vital signs, physical examination findings.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially said “both knees” hurt; later clarified pain localized to right knee—conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
